question: Find the value of $k$ for which the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(2\hat{i}+\hat{j})+\mu(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+k\hat{k})$ are coplanar.
explanation:
Step 1: Identification of the vectors
For the first line,
$$\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{k},\quad \vec{b}_1=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$$
For the second line,
$$\vec{a}_2=2\hat{i}+\hat{j},\quad \vec{b}_2=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+k\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Vector joining points on the lines
$$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Coplanarity condition
The lines are coplanar when
$$\left(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2\right)=0.$$
Step 4: Evaluation of the scalar triple product
$$\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2=(2k-1)\hat{i}-(k+2)\hat{j}-5\hat{k}.$$
Hence,
$$1(2k-1)+1(-k-2)+(-1)(-5)=0.$$
This gives
$$2k-1-k-2+5=0\Rightarrow k+2=0.$$
Step 5: Final result
Therefore, the required value is $k=-2$.
